trigger: Residual Marshall sorties plus the Independence torpedo hit demonstrate that the first suppression cycle did not sterilize the network.

US_adaptation.extra_fast_carrier_offensive_sorties: ~45-65 reallocated late 11/23 and dawn 11/24, mainly Taroa/Mili/Jaluit staging and airfield systems
US_adaptation.extra_land_based_attack_search_sorties: ~15-25, including repeat runway/base-system work and reconnaissance
US_adaptation.fighter_reservation: ~20-30 additional F6F-equivalent deck positions/cycles tied to CAP/sweep/escort during the dangerous window
US_adaptation.cost: less discretionary search/secondary-target work and less immediate fast-deck flexibility; assault CVEs take a larger share of local CAS/ASW/spotting

Japanese_network_at_1943_11_24_dawn.land_fighters_immediate_ready: ~36-45 across Marshall/Gilbert staging nodes, excluding aircraft merely repairable
Japanese_network_at_1943_11_24_dawn.attack_aircraft_immediate_ready: ~5-9 after D-1 strike losses and repeat suppression
Japanese_network_at_1943_11_24_dawn.note: This remains a dangerous search/CAP/nuisance network but no longer supports a second 20+ aircraft torpedo strike immediately at dawn.

base_state.Taroa: runway intermittent/repairing; C2 survives in fragments; ~9-13 fighters immediate-ready and 0-2 attack aircraft
base_state.Mili: degraded but usable; ~4-6 fighters, 2-4 attack, 1-2 Kyofu, Zuiun/search residue
base_state.Jaluit: runway low-output; water-air support partially intact; 3-5 water/recon fighters/search assets remain usable
base_state.Nauru: 0-2 immediate-ready, mostly emergency/local; repair system survives better than air combat system
base_state.Tarawa: normal runway combat operations effectively closed; surviving flyable air largely evacuated/staged

strategic_result: US adapts successfully enough to protect the landing, but pays additional deck/sortie workload and cannot simultaneously maximize island CAS, Marshall suppression, fleet CAP/search and ASW.
